chunks: And what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who has a wife with him, is it permissible for him to marry her sister in mut'ah (temporary marriage)? He said, 'No.' I said, 'Zurarah narrated from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), "It is like the female slaves; he may marry whomever he wishes."' He said, 'No, she is one of the four [prohibited sisters].'

So these two reports are not contradictory to what we have previously mentioned from the reports, because these two reports came in the context of precaution (ihtiyat) rather than prohibition, and that which clarifies what we mentioned is what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is temporary marriage between two sisters permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* resolves a juristic nuance regarding temporary marriage (*Mut'ah*) between sisters by distinguishing between absolute prohibition and precautionary caution (*ihtiyat*). While some reports likened the flexibility of *Mut'ah* to slavery, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that sisters remain among the four primary prohibitions, ensuring the ruling aligns with the broader principle of avoiding simultaneous marriage to two sisters even in temporary contracts.
